raw_case_text:
A 47-year-old married male with acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) who was a shopkeeper by profession presented with skin lesions on both lower limbs for past 9 months. It was associated with mild itching and pain. There were no complaints of joint pain or redness of eyes. The patient was diagnosed with HIV in 2007 and first-line antiretroviral therapy (ART) (tenofovir, lamivudine, efavirenz) was started in 2009. He developed severe fatigue, weight loss, cough, and dyspnea, and CD4 count dropped to 50 cells/mm3 with plasma viral load of 157 copies/ml, 11 months ago in March 2015. Due to treatment failure, he was then put on second-line ART (abacavir, lamivudine, atazanavir, and ritonavir) and his CD4 count increased to 204 cells/mm3 with plasma viral load of 38 copies/ml in September 2015. The present skin lesions started 2 months after initiation of second-line ART. Patient also had history of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) in 2007 when his CD4 count was 213 cells/mm3, and Herpes Zoster in 2012 when CD4 count was 78 for which treatment was taken.
On general examination, patient was moderately built and nourished, and his vitals were within normal limits. Cutaneous examination revealed multiple well-defined nontender hyperpigmented papules and nodules on both ankles, dorsum of bilateral feet and soles [Figure 1a-c]. Inguinal lymph nodes were not palpable. There were no lesions elsewhere in the body. Hair, nail, and oral mucosa were normal. No ocular or systemic abnormality was noted.
Differential diagnoses considered were Kaposi's sarcoma and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) related infection including cutaneous TB. His routine blood investigations showed hemoglobin 11.5 g%, total leukocyte count 4300/mm3; and differential count neutrophil 70%, lymphocytes 28%, eosinophils 1% and monocytes 1%, and platelets 287,000/mm3. Liver function tests and renal function tests were normal. Mantoux test, serological tests for syphilis (VDRL, TPHA), hepatitis B and C, and anti-nuclear antibodies were negative. Chest radiography and abdominal ultrasonography were normal. Biopsy taken from the nodular lesion on dorsum of left foot showed a diffused dense infiltrate in reticular dermis with mild fibroplasia. The infiltrate consisted of neutrophils and histiocytes with scattering of lymphocytes and plasma cells. The infiltrate surrounded small thickened vessels and extended extensively into the interstitium. Small amount of neutrophilic nuclear dust was also present within the infiltrate [Figure 2]. Overlying epidermis and dermoepidermal junction were largely spared. These features were suggestive of EED. Patient was started on oral dapsone 100 mg/day and then increased to 200 mg/day to which he is responding gradually.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 47-year-old married male shopkeeper with AIDS presented with a 9-month history of mildly pruritic and painful hyperpigmented papules and nodules over both lower extremities.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with HIV in 2007 and started on first-line ART (tenofovir, lamivudine, efavirenz) in 2009, the patient experienced immunological failure in March 2015 (CD4 count 50 cells/mm3, viral load 157 copies/mL) with fatigue, weight loss, cough, and dyspnea, prompting switch to second-line ART (abacavir, lamivudine, atazanavir, and ritonavir). Two months after starting second-line ART (9 months prior to presentation, as his CD4 count rose to 204 cells/mm3), he developed persistent mildly itchy and painful papules and nodules over both ankles, dorsal feet, and soles.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV/AIDS diagnosed in 2007; pulmonary tuberculosis in 2007 (at CD4 count 213 cells/mm3, treated); herpes zoster in 2012 (at CD4 count 78 cells/mm3, treated); switched from first-line TDF/3TC/EFV to second-line abacavir/lamivudine/atazanavir/ritonavir 11 months prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for lower extremity skin nodules with mild pruritus and pain; negative for arthralgias or ocular redness. Home medications: abacavir, lamivudine, atazanavir, and ritonavir.

objective.physical_examination: Moderately built and nourished with normal vital signs. Cutaneous examination revealed multiple well-defined, non-tender, hyperpigmented papules and nodules symmetrically distributed over both ankles, the dorsum of both feet, and the soles, without inguinal lymphadenopathy or mucosal, nail, hair, or ocular lesions.
objective.routine_investigations: Routine blood tests showed hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL, WBC 4,300/mm3 (70% neutrophils, 28% lymphocytes, 1% eosinophils, 1% monocytes), platelets 287,000/mm3, and normal liver and renal function tests. Mantoux test, VDRL, TPHA, HBsAg, anti-HCV, and ANA were all negative. Chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound were normal.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count had increased from 50 cells/mm3 in March 2015 to 204 cells/mm3 in September 2015. Skin biopsy from a left dorsal foot nodule demonstrated a spared epidermis/dermoepidermal junction and a dense diffuse reticular dermal infiltrate of neutrophils and histiocytes with scattered lymphocytes, plasma cells, leukocytoclasis (nuclear dust), mild fibroplasia, and thickened small dermal vessels diagnostic of erythema elevatum diutinum (EED).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Erythema elevatum diutinum (EED) presenting 2 months after initiation of protease-inhibitor-based second-line antiretroviral therapy (abacavir, lamivudine, atazanavir, and ritonavir; CD4+ count rising from 50 to 204 cells/mm3, plasma HIV viral load 38 copies/mL) in a 47-year-old male with AIDS. Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous tuberculosis were ruled out by characteristic leukocytoclastic vasculitic/fibroplastic dermal histopathology. Oral dapsone was initiated at 100 mg/day and titrated to 200 mg/day alongside continued second-line ART, resulting in gradual regression of the acral nodules.
